study type: Post hoc secondary observational analysis of a community-based, cluster-randomized controlled trial
exposure: Use of individual clean delivery kit (CDK) components (soap, gloves, cord clamps, plastic sheet, razor blade, matches, candle)
outcome: Perinatal mortality (stillbirth plus neonatal death in the first 7 days of life)
cohort: The study analyzed 36,996 newborns from 38,579 deliveries of pregnant women who participated in the Zambia Chlorhexidine Application Trial (ZamCAT) in Southern Province of Zambia.
finding: The use of several clean delivery kit (CDK) components, specifically gloves, cord clamps, plastic sheets, and razor blades, was significantly associated with a lower risk of newborn mortality.
